findings.title: Unauthenticated Presigned Upload Credential Acquisition
findings.cwe_id: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
findings.description: The application allows anonymous, unauthenticated clients to request valid presigned upload URLs/policies. An attacker can abuse this endpoint to obtain unauthorized cloud storage write credentials.
findings.recommendation: Implement mandatory authentication and authorization checks (e.g. Bearer token or session cookie validation) before generating presigned upload credentials.

findings.title: Excessive Presigned Upload TTL (604800s (~7.0 days))
findings.description: The presigned upload credential has an excessively long validity period of 604800s (~7.0 days), exceeding the safe threshold of 300 seconds. Long-lived presigned credentials increase the exposure window if leaked or intercepted.
findings.recommendation: Configure the presigned URL/policy TTL to a short window (e.g., 300 seconds / 5 minutes) sufficient only for completing the immediate client upload.

findings.category: V3: Unrestricted File Types and File Size
findings.title: Unrestricted File Types and File Size Allowed
findings.cwe_id: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
findings.description: The application and presigned storage policy lack critical upload boundaries: maximum file size limits (permits arbitrary DoS payloads), Content-Type / MIME restrictions (permits dangerous executable payloads).

missing_constraints: maximum file size limits (permits arbitrary DoS payloads)
Content-Type / MIME restrictions (permits dangerous executable payloads)

findings.recommendation: Implement server-side MIME whitelisting, enforce size validation during presigned URL generation, and embed ['content-length-range', 1, <max_bytes>] conditions in POST policies.

findings.title: Predictable Storage Key Naming Allows Arbitrary File Overwrite
findings.cwe_id: CWE-73: External Control of File Name or Path
findings.description: The backend dispatches static, un-namespaced object keys (e.g. 'uploads/audit_probe_sample.txt') directly derived from client-supplied filenames. An attacker can overwrite other users' stored files by uploading a file with the same filename.
findings.recommendation: Prepend a cryptographically random UUID or secure hash to storage keys (e.g., 'uploads/{uuid4()}_{filename}') to prevent key collisions and unauthorized overwriting.

findings.category: V5: File Stealing & Unauthorized Public Read
findings.title: Uploaded Files Publicly Accessible via Unauthenticated Read
findings.cwe_id: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
findings.description: Uploaded files are stored with 'public-read' access permissions (HTTP 403). Any unauthenticated third party with knowledge or guessing of the object key can download sensitive user data without authorization (File Stealing risk).
findings.recommendation: Enforce 'private' ACL on all uploaded objects and serve files exclusively through authenticated application endpoints or short-lived presigned download URLs.

findings.title: Callback Notification Spoofing Vulnerability Detected
findings.cwe_id: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
findings.description: The backend accepted a fabricated upload callback (HTTP 200) for a non-existent object without validating cryptographic signatures or verifying that the file was actually written to cloud storage. An attacker can forge database entries, trigger post-processing workflows, or falsify transaction confirmations.

response_body.message: Upload recorded and registered in application database.

findings.recommendation: Require HMAC-signed tokens in callback requests and perform server-side object verification (e.g. s3.head_object) to confirm object existence and byte size before registering the upload.
